lede: US stocks fell sharply on Friday, with the S&P 500 down 3.7% to 6,910.39, which put it in a correction after a seventh straight daily loss.

items.title: Corpay to invest $1.1 billion for about a third of BILL in a TPG-led $6 billion buyout
facts: BILL will be bought for $63.25 per share in cash, valuing it at about $6.0 billion; TPG takes a majority stake and Corpay a minority.
Corpay has an option to buy the remaining shares in 2030; closing is expected in the first half of 2027.
items.why: Shows a large payments company taking a stake in a business-payments platform through a private equity deal.

items.title: BILL Holdings agrees to a take-private by TPG with Corpay at $63.25 per share
facts: The cash price is a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average price before reports of talks.
Board approved unanimously; Starboard Value, the largest shareholder, agreed to vote in favor.
items.why: A take-private at a premium is a signal for valuations in financial software and payments.

items.title: Boston Scientific prices $3 billion of US notes and €4.25 billion of euro notes
facts: The dollar notes come in four tranches, with coupons from 5.375% (due 2029) to 5.875% (due 2036).
The euro notes, issued by a subsidiary and guaranteed by the company, run from floating rate due 2028 to 5.125% due 2046; closing is set for Dec. 1.
items.why: A large bond sale in both currencies; the special redemption terms suggest it funds an acquisition.

items.title: Take-Two keeps its fiscal 2027 net bookings outlook at $8 billion to $8.2 billion as GTA VI launches
facts: At its Nov. 9 results, the company kept the outlook and confirmed the Grand Theft Auto VI release for Nov. 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
It guided third-quarter diluted net income to $1.30 to $1.44 per share.
items.why: The launch of one of the largest video game titles of the year bears on the company's bookings.

items.title: S&P 500 falls 3.7% and closes in a correction as the Nasdaq drops 5.3%
facts: Friday's close: S&P 500 down 3.7% to 6,910.39; Dow down about 1.9% to 48,147.33; Nasdaq Composite down 5.28% to 22,617.73.
The Nasdaq Composite is now below its level at the start of 2026; the S&P 500 lost 7 sessions in a row.
items.why: A 10%-plus pullback from the peak marks an official correction; chip and AI infrastructure shares led the declines.

items.title: Worst week since April 2025: S&P 500 down 8.6%, Dow down 8%, volatility gauge near 36
facts: The S&P 500 lost 8.6% over the week, its biggest weekly drop since April 2025; the Dow lost about 8%.
One digest put the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) at 35.89, up about 26% on the day.
items.why: Large weekly losses and a high VIX show how fast risk appetite shifted away from AI-linked stocks.

watch.what: US stock markets closed for Thanksgiving Day
